Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Government revenue collection via digital channels is evidenced for customs ePayment: SRC launched an online payment facility for Customs services (government revenue stream) and an ePayment form is provided for customs declaration payments. This indicates partial digital revenue collection (at least customs).

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Tax portal / e-services exist: Seychelles Nation explains SRC “taxation e-service” allowing employers to submit monthly payroll online via an e-service gateway (24/7) with e-ID/password/access code. Evidence is about e-filing/submission (payroll declarations) rather than full tax payment portal, but indicates an operational tax e-service portal.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: B2B payments are supported via SEFT domestic bank transfers (used for business payments and remittance within Seychelles). Bank of Baroda notes SEFT is “an electronic domestic funds transfer system setup between all banks in Seychelles” for secure transfers to any bank/credit union, usable by customers/merchants (SEFT Phase II). This supports business-to-business transfers via bank accounts.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: P2B merchant payments exist: Airtel Money launch coverage states users can “shop at a variety of merchant outlets” and pay utility bills, and 2012 CBS mobile payments project description envisaged P2B real-time mobile payments; additionally, SEFT Phase II supports customer or merchant registration per Bank of Baroda SEFT page.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government (P2G) digital payments exist at least for customs: Seychelles Postal Regulator provides an online “ePayment” form to pay customs declaration; and SRC announced launch of an “online payment facility for Customs services” (Automated System for Customs Data enhancement). This is active P2G for a major government payment stream.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P functionality exists via both bank transfers (SEFT) and mobile money. Seychelles Nation reports Airtel Money (launched 2015) enables users to “load cash… send and receive money” via mobile. SEFT customer manual shows customers can create payments to customers of any commercial bank/SCU via SEFT.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: CBS directly operates core payment infrastructure: CBS states it is “a payment system operator and banker to Government” on its AML/CFT compliance page, and CBS press communiqué on SEFT upgrade identifies CBS as “the operator of the system”. This indicates direct operation rather than only regulation.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Seychelles has a dedicated financial consumer protection framework covering payments: CBS consumer laws page states the Financial Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) was assented to 14 April 2022 with commencement 1 May 2022, aimed at handling financial consumer disputes and protecting financial consumers. Complaint-handling regulations under the FCPA (S.I. 110 of 2024) apply to all financial services providers including payment service providers and require complaint handling units and processes.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Seychelles has an operational nationwide domestic electronic funds transfer system, SEFT (Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer). CBS press releases state SEFT was “officially launched on August 19, 2013 by the Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS), being the operator of the system” and enables domestic funds transfers; later upgrades integrated banks for straight-through processing (immediate debit/credit) and enabled broader customer access. The SEFT customer manual shows the SEFT service used by customers of commercial banks and the Seychelles Credit Union via https://www.seychelleseft.sc, indicating broad deployment.
